thread.title: Tech Today: Nasdaq Down 1%, Pondering VMware, Handicapping Broadcom

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Nasdaq Down 1%, Pondering VMware, Handicapping Broadcom
text:
Here are some things going on today in your world of tech :
The Nasdaq Composite is down 1% at the open, falling along with other major indices. Losses are across the board.
VMware caught in Dell story Shares of virtualization pioneer VMware ( VMW ) are down $7.64, or 6%, at $116.02, despite the company yesterday afternoon beating fiscal Q4 expectations, and affirming its outlook: as William Blair 's Jason Ader writes, it was a "strong" report, but it doesn't really matter. "VMware stock has now become event-driven," with Michael Dell 's rumored interest in conducting a reverse merger . "The strong current fundamentals matter less," he concludes.
Nutanix, Pure Rising Shares of "hyper-converged" technology pioneer Nutanix ( NTNX ) are one stock bucking the weak market, up 96 cents, or 2.7%, at $37.16, in early trading, after the company yesterday afternoon reported fiscal Q2 results that topped analysts' expectations, and forecast this quarter's results higher as well. CEO Dheeraj Pandey told me his company's transition to being a software-only shop is going well.
Piper Jaffray 's Andrew Nowinski agrees. He reiterates an Overweight rating this morning, and a $44 price target, "Nutanix continues to execute well, effectively transitioning to a software-only model, which should ultimately lead to an acceleration in revenue growth and profitability."
Shares of storage technology vendor Pure Storage ( PSTG ) are down $2.13, or 10%, at $19.65, despite the fact the company beat with its fiscal Q4, and delivered its first profitable quarter ever. CEO Charles Giancarlo was unfazed about the stock drop , and when I asked what was most significant about the quarter, he said ""I think it's quite straightforward: We just crossed a billion dollars as a company."
The sell-off, write the analysts today, is a result of a lower-than-expected gross profit margin , but analysts point out that's because the newer " FlashBlade " product is still young. "The company should begin to see improved cost efficiencies on this product as it matures," writes Piper's Nowinski.
Srini Nandury of Summit Insights Group thinks "investors should use any weakness to accumulate shares."
Upgrading Splunk Another gainer from yesterday is Splunk ( SPLK ), the data analysis company, whose shares are up $3.50, or almost 4%, at $97.14. after its fiscal Q4 results easily topped expectations, and its outlook beat as well.
The shares have gotten one upgrade today, that I can see, from Stifel Nicolaus 's Brad Reback , who raises his rating to Buy from Hold, and hikes his target all the way to $120 from $75, writing that the quarter "indicates the company is successfully pivoting its business model toward subscription revenue (on-prem and cloud)."
Snap priced to perfection Needham & Co .'s Laura Martin writes today there are many things to like about Snap, including the company's recent redesign of Snapchat , which is binding in an older audience, and things it has done to fix its Android version.
But she continues to rate the stock Underperform, given it is "priced for perfection at nearly 20 times fiscal 2018 estimated sales." She'd rather buy Facebook ( FB ), she writes.
Snap shares today are down 34 cents, or 2%, at $16.87.
SEC perusing coin offerings The Securities & Exchange Commission is cracking down on crypto-currencies , according to a report this morning from The New York Posts 's Kevin Dugan and Carleton English , citing multiple unnamed sources. The SEC has been sending subpoenas to various companies offering so-called initial coin offerings , offers to the public to buy into the currencies. You'll recall Eastman Kodak (KODK) in January announced an ICO for its "Kodak Coins."
The overarching theme of the "crackdown," the writers relate, is that the SEC views the currencies as securities , as opposed to coin backers' contention they are "utilities." That could impose restrictions about insider trading in the offerings, Dugan and English offer.
Samsung Galaxy fizzle, iPhone X Slump Samsung Electronics 's ( 005930KS ) has " Galaxy S9 ," unveiled at the mobile world congress in Barcelona on Sunday, has met with lower-than-expected demand since they went on sales as pre-order on Wednesday, coming in below pre-order rates for their predecessors, according to a report from the Yonhap News Agency , citing "industry watchers."
Samsung shares, at a recent 2,301,000, are down 2.5% this week.
Samsung need not feel too bad: Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman and Sam Kim today add more fuel to the case that Apple 's (AAPL) iPhone X isn't living up to expectations. They report Samsung, the supplier of the OLED screens for the device, is going to ship "about half the units planed" to Apple, without specifying a time frame, citing unnamed sources.
Apple stock is down $1.27, or 0.7%, at $173.73.
Upgrading Microchip The Street is assessing yesterday afternoon's announcement by chip maker Microchip Technology (MCHP) that it will buy fellow semiconductor maker Microsemi (MSCC) for a total of $10 billion.
Most of the responses are lukewarm. Mizuho 's Vijay Rakesh, who has a Neutral rating on Microchip shares, writes that there is "little overlap" between the two, but also "little strategic value" in the deal. Similarly, Susquehanna 's Christopher Rolland , who has a "Positive" rating on Microchip, "applauds the deal," but he thinks its "impetus is more likely financially motivated rather than strategic."
But SunTrust 's William Stein raises his rating on Microchip to Buy from Hold, writing that "MSCC will be significantly accretive and will ultimately exceed management's guidance."
The move has boosted Microchip stock, which is up $3.22, or 3.6%, at $92.24.
Lam's analyst meeting Speaking of chips, chip equipment maker Lam Research (LRCX) will hold its annual analyst briefing in New York City next Tuesday, March 6th ( info here ), and Craig Ellis with B. Riley reiterates his Buy rating, and his $270 price target, writing that the "We believe the stage is set for an upbeat tone on industry fundy's."
He raises the possibly there may be "indications" the company's revenue and profit could rise to $13 billion and $20 a share come 2020. And then there's that $5 billion in cash and billions in cash flow that open up "significant value creation."
Lam shares today are down $5.14, or 2.7%, at $184.93.
D-day looms for Qualcomm, Broadcom You know what else happens next Tuesday? Qualcomm (QCOM) holds it annual shareholder meeting, where there's a showdown between it and Broadcom (AVGO), which is attempting a hostile takeover of Qualcomm and which has asked Qualcomm shareholders to vote in its six nominees to the board of directors.
Srinni Pajjuri with Macquarie Research is pounding the table for Broadcom shares, saying you pretty much can't lose come Tuesday. Even if Broadcom has the worst outcome - losing the vote but continuing the fight -- "we do not see much downside given the depressed valuation," writes Pajjuri.
Qualcomm shares today are down 67 cents, or 1%, at $64.29, while Broadcom shares are down $1.59, or 0.7%, at $241.72.
